messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: High error rate + latency on kv-shard-tp pool. Symptoms: NCCL stalls detected, KV cache growth spike, continuous-batching queue backlog. Auto-escalated to on-call.

Ryan O'Neill (oncall): I'm on it. @Maria / @Jay can you confirm which changes went live in the last hour? Link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-tp 

Maria Chen: saw a config roll earlier from jay: batcher.max_token_window=2048 -> 8192 and kv.shard_strategy=auto->tensor-parallel. Rollout started 40m ago.

Jay Patel: yep that was the batching/kv-shard roll for perf experiments. we enabled larger token windows to reduce RPC count. rolling back now if needed.

Olivia Park: metrics: kv-cache size per-gpu jumped 3x on tp-shard-XX nodes, NCCL error rate up, and the scheduler shows heavy cross-gpu ops. Looks like uneven partitioning: some shards have 70% of items.

Ryan O'Neill (oncall): Customer impact? @Amy?

Amy Torres: CS reports increased 503s for two large customers (acct-47, acct-102) starting ~1839991800. Estimated affected requests ~4k over 10m. They're seeing timeouts and retries.

Maria Chen: logs show repeated NCCL timeout messages and kernel queue saturation. snippet: ```[2026-07-09T12:12:45Z] ERROR nccl: NCCL timeout on ring 1, rank 2 -> peer blocked```

Jay Patel: hypothesis: tensor-parallel sharding algorithm assigned heavy KV keys to same GPU due to hash collision exacerbated by larger token window. continuous batching amplified hot keys and filled KV cache on a subset of GPUs causing NCCL sync stalls.

Ryan O'Neill (oncall): action plan: 1) pause kv-shard tensor-parallel mode -> fallback to balanced-shard; 2) reduce batcher.max_token_window back to 2048; 3) drain/evict hot cache entries; 4) restart affected tp-shard pods gradually. who can run the config revert?

Jay Patel: I'm rolling the revert now. curl to control plane: ```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://control.redwood/api/v1/configs/kv-shard -d '{"strategy":"balanced-shard"}'``` then apply batching rollback: ```curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/configs/batcher -d '{"max_token_window":2048}'```

deploy-bot: deploy started: config/kv-shard@rev-20260709-rollback by jay (job-id dply-78321). Canarying on pool tp-shard-a (2 nodes).

Olivia Park: running eviction: `redis-cli -h kv-hotspot flushkey keypattern:hot*` on the two overloaded GPUs' local cache instances. Starting eviction now.

Maria Chen: also toggling continuous-batching to conservative mode: `batcher.mode=latency-first`. This should prevent large intra-request batches from forming.

Ryan O'Neill (oncall): good. watch nccl/errors, queue lengths, and 5xx rate. update in 5.

(5 minutes later)

Olivia Park: metrics trending: NCCL error rate dropping, queue backlog decreased 80% on canary nodes. Latency back to baseline on canary.

deploy-bot: deploy success: config/kv-shard@rev-20260709-rollback applied to tp-shard-a. Rolling to tp-shard-b.

Amy Torres: acct-47 seeing recovery now. They'll keep smoke testing and we told them we're rolling a fix.

Jay Patel: rolling to remaining tp-shard pools. ETA ~12m for full roll.

incident-bot: ALERT suppressed: kv-shard-tp NCCL-stall spikes cleared on canary nodes.

Ryan O'Neill (oncall): All pools rolled. Confirming final checks: 1) NCCL errors ~0, 2) per-gpu kv-cache sizes normalized, 3) 5xx rate back to baseline.

Olivia Park: all good on metrics. No new NCCL timeouts in last 10m.

Amy Torres: CS confirmed both customers restored and asked for incident summary/eta for postmortem.

Maria Chen: immediate mitigation done. Root cause hypothesis: tensor-parallel shard allocator produced skew under new hash window when combined with large batch token window; continuous batching amplified hot-key pressure causing local KV caches to exceed expected residency and trigger heavy cross-GPU syncs/NCCL stalls.

Jay Patel: follow-ups: 1) add fast-detect rule for uneven kv-shard distribution (alert if per-gpu cache imbalance > 2x), 2) add canary gate for kv-shard strategy changes, 3) ensure batching experiments run on isolated test pools first. I'll open tickets.

Ryan O'Neill (oncall): I'll file the incident and schedule a postmortem with eng-runtime + SRE + CS. Please add timeline and actions (eviction command, config revs, roll IDs).

Maria Chen: note for postmortem: also test combining large token window with tp sharding in perf lab. We should have a cheap synthetic load to reproduce hot-key amplification.

Jay Patel: created tickets: INF-4821 (kv-shard imbalance alert), INF-4822 (canary gating), INF-4823 (perf-lab test).

Ryan O'Neill (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in 10. @Olivia you'll own final write-up with metrics and runbook updates. @Maria/Jay own follow-ups. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Olivia Park: ack. I'll draft summary and upload graphs.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. Severity: Sev2. Duration: ~18m. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-07-10 16:00 UTC.
